agree.reason: An owner who pays her cousin $600 a year sees $199 a month on the page, never sees the cost set against what she pays now, and has no reason given to move the work away from family, so she is unlikely to book the call.

honest.reason: Every figure matches the brief and the claims are hedged where they should be (the missed deadlines, 'I can't promise'); the page leaves out the January price rise but doesn't say anything false about it.

works_the_facts.reason: The page repeats the raw figures but works none of them out: it never gives the annual cost ($2,388), the on-time rate (9 of 12 closes), the share of clients who saw a lower accountant bill (9 of 31), or the fact that no client left because they were unhappy.

right_comparison.reason: The reader's real alternative is a once-a-year cleanup for $600 with no monthly books, payroll or sales tax filing, and the page never describes that alternative or sets its own offer against it.

qualification.reason: The 10th-of-the-month deadline and the accountant-savings hedge are both checkable, but neither says what happens to the client when the date is missed or the savings don't come.

objections.reason: The page answers objections the reader never raised (missed deadlines, the one-person setup) but doesn't answer the one she has: why pay roughly four times what her cousin charges.

fit.reason: It runs about 370 words, has clear sales-page sections, and ends with the booking button the brief asked for.
